title: Pointer sample fields
description: Fields every pointer message carries. Each message is self-contained: absolute position AND the absolute button mask, never a delta and never an event the receiver has to accumulate. That is what makes the unordered/unreliable channel survivable -- a lost packet degrades to a late repair rather than permanently wrong state.

seq.description: Monotonic per channel, one stream for every pointer message type. The receiver drops a move whose seq it has already passed (the channel reorders) and drops a button transition older than the last one applied for that button.

t.description: Sender's clock in ms (Date.now()). Diagnostics only -- never used for ordering, because the two clocks are unsynchronised.

nx.description: Horizontal position as a fraction of the rendered video frame. Normalised rather than pixels so a resolution change on the desktop cannot invalidate an in-flight packet; the phone never learns the desktop resolution. See docs/ui-spec.md section 4.

ny.description: Vertical position, same basis as nx.

buttons.description: Bitmask of buttons held AFTER this event: 1 left, 2 right, 4 middle. Same values as DOM MouseEvent.buttons. Present on moves too, which is how a lost pointerUp repairs itself: the next move disagrees with what the host holds, and the host reconciles.
